findings.description: storage_encrypted is set to false, so the RDS MySQL instance and its underlying storage/snapshots store data in plaintext.
publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, greatly expanding attack surface for a database that should be private.
The master username is the default 'admin', which is a well-known target for credential guessing/brute-force attacks against the publicly exposed database.
The master password is supplied through var.password and is stored in plaintext in Terraform state and is reused in EC2 user data; no secrets manager or managed password is used.
No enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit/error/general/slowquery) and no IAM database authentication are configured, so database access is not auditable.
The user_data script embeds the database master username and password in cleartext; user data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstances or via the instance metadata service.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains available and an SSRF in the hosted PHP app could retrieve the instance role's credentials (which are near-admin for S3/EC2/RDS).
No root_block_device/ebs_block_device encryption is specified, so the instance volumes containing the credential file /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc may be unencrypted at rest.
The instance is launched in a subnet and exposes a public DNS name (output db_app_public_dns), placing an internet-facing web server with a privileged instance profile directly on the internet.
The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", effectively administrative control over storage, compute, and databases for any compromise of the EC2 instance.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the RDS security group, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel.
The RDS security group has no explicit restrictive rules of its own and pairs with a fully open egress rule; combined with publicly_accessible on the database, network layering is not enforced.
The parameter group does not set require_secure_transport (or equivalent), so unencrypted MySQL client connections to the publicly reachable database are permitted.
